title: RecorderSegment - a contiguous capture interval and its integrity verdict
description: The unit a consumer accepts or rejects. Carries the gap ledger that ADR-003 requires, because the client library reconnects silently and never tells the caller a discontinuity happened.

sourceMix.description: ADR-006: a segment assembled from more than one source declares every source. A consumer may reject a mixed segment.

subscriptionScope.description: Without this, sequence statistics are uninterpretable. A per-price MBO subscription sees a SPARSE SLICE of a book-wide counter, so a large span with few distinct values is expected and is NOT loss (ADR-002).

sequenceStats.description: Three DISTINCT measurements. Sorting the sequence before counting gaps destroys arrival order and was a defect in an earlier probe; arrivalInversions is what detects reordering.

missingWithinSpan.description: span - distinct. This is NOT a loss count unless subscriptionScope.kind is instrument_wide.

containsUnrecoveredGap.description: ADR-003. True whenever any discontinuity coincided with a connection event. Never cleared by attaching historical backfill.

discontinuities.description: One entry per connection-coincident sequence break. Measured example: 115664320 -> 115668295 across a 12.4 s outage, delta 3975, unrecovered.

recoveryAttempted.description: Always false today: no gap-fill request exists in this protocol path.

recoveryMechanism.description: Constrained to a single value so that a future mechanism cannot be claimed without a schema change and a decision record.

unparseableFrameCount.description: ADR-007: counted per segment, not logged per frame.

gapToleranceRef.description: DQ-001's tolerance. Unbound today - ADR-005 forbids inventing it. Degraded-vs-Invalid classification on non-connection gaps is therefore NOT available, which is why a connection-coincident gap goes straight to Invalid (needs no threshold).

then.description: ADR-003: an unrecovered gap forces Invalid and the DATA_INVALID reason code, and at least one discontinuity record must be present. This is the fail-closed rule expressed in the schema rather than left to the writer.
Ready forbids an unrecovered gap. A recorder that cannot determine gap state must not emit Ready.
